questions.question: For \(f(x)=x^3\), JAX reports \(f\prime(0)=0\). What can you conclude?
options: The first-order local slope is zero; optimality requires more evidence.
JAX has stopped differentiating because the output is zero.
questions.explanation: The cubic is stationary at zero but takes smaller values to the left. A zero first derivative alone does not prove a minimum.
optionFeedback: A zero first derivative is compatible with a maximum, minimum or stationary inflection. Compare nearby values on both sides of zero.
The cubic is stationary at zero but takes smaller values to the left. A zero first derivative alone does not prove a minimum.
The derivative is zero because the function is locally flat to first order at this input. Differentiate at a nonzero input to check the rule.
